Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "MinebeaMitsumi Inc."
Document: "Minebea Co., Ltd."

Minebea Co., Ltd. is the historical name — MinebeaMitsumi Inc. was formed in 2017 when Minebea acquired Mitsumi Electric and renamed itself. The certificate is from 2011, when the company was legally named "Minebea Co., Ltd." So the register's value is the modern/current name of the same corporate entity, while the document's value is the legal name at issuance time.

The certificate is the legal instrument, so which value should the fused record carry? The rules say: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. Genuinely different company names = different-entity with best_value = document's.

Is "Minebea Co., Ltd." vs "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." the same entity? Yes, it's the same corporate entity — the company renamed itself. But the rules say "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Hmm. Is this "genuinely different"? The names differ because of a corporate rename over time. But the certificate as a legal instrument in 2011 named "Minebea Co., Ltd." as the applicant. The register apparently normalized/updated the name to the current name "MinebeaMitsumi Inc."

The rules don't explicitly cover temporal renaming. But I think the intent: same entity (company rename isn't a different company). However, the verdict options are: same-entity, different-entity, document-noise, unverifiable.

A corporate rename is arguably the same entity — the entity is identical, just a name change over time. "Genuinely different company" would be like "Minebea Co., Ltd." vs "Acme Weighing B.V." Here it's clearly the same company.

But for best_value: which should the fused record carry? The rules say for same-entity cases involving number/year format differences, use register's canonical form. For spelling drift/suffix drift = same-entity — presumably keep document's value since certificate is legal instrument? Actually rules don't say what best_value is for spelling drift. Presumably either.

Given the certificate is the legal instrument, and the document says "Minebea Co., Ltd." as of 2011, the fused record should arguably carry the document's value since that's what the certificate legally states. However, register canonicalization to the current entity name "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." could be considered the canonical form for linking.

The rule: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)." If I treat this as same-entity, no explicit best_value rule, but I'd say document's value because it's the legal name at time of issuance. Hmm, but many fusion systems would prefer the register's normalized current name.

Actually, let me reconsider. The register says "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." — this is the current legal name (since 2017). The document says "Minebea Co., Ltd." — the legal name in 2011. Same corporate entity, temporal name drift. This is analogous to legal-suffix drift / name drift — same entity.

Best value: I'd argue the document's value "Minebea Co., Ltd." because the certificate is the legal instrument and the applicant named on the certificate in 2011 was Minebea Co., Ltd. The register's value is an anachronistic normalization. So verdict: same-entity, best_value: "Minebea Co., Ltd.".

Hmm, but one could argue the register's canonical form is preferred for consistency. The rules only prefer register's canonical form for number/year format differences. For same-entity name conflicts, the certificate being the legal instrument suggests document value wins. Also note the extraction_method header itself lists applicant as "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." — that's from the register/extraction metadata embedded in the doc context, not the certificate text. The certificate's visible text says "Minebea Co., Ltd."

So: verdict "same-entity", best_value "Minebea Co., Ltd.", why: it's the same corporate entity under its legal name at issuance (renamed to MinebeaMitsumi in 2017), and the certificate as legal instrument carries the 2011 name.

Alternatively verdict "different-entity"? No — it's genuinely the same company; calling it different-entity would be wrong factually. The rules' "different-entity" is for genuinely different companies.

I'll go with same-entity, best_value from document. One short sentence.
